message.content:
**Los Angeles (Pacific Time) vs. Berlin (Central European Time)**  

| Period | LA Time Zone | Berlin Time Zone | Difference | Notes |
|--------|--------------|------------------|------------|-------|
| **Standard Time** (winter) | UTC‑8 | UTC+1 | **9 hours** (Berlin ahead) | Both are on “standard” time. |
| **Daylight‑Saving Time** (summer) | UTC‑7 | UTC+2 | **9 hours** (Berlin ahead) | Both are on DST, so the offset stays 9 h. |
| **Transition windows** | | | | |
| Early March (after US DST starts, before EU DST starts) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **8 hours** (Berlin ahead) | US DST begins 2 weeks earlier than EU DST. |
| Late October/early November (after EU DST ends, before US DST ends) | UTC‑7 | UTC+1 | **8 hours** (Berlin ahead) | EU DST ends 1 week earlier than US DST. |

**Bottom line:**  
- For most of the year, Berlin is **9 hours ahead** of Los Angeles.  
- During the short overlap periods when one region has switched to DST and the other has not, the gap shrinks to **8 hours**.  

If you’re planning a call, just double‑check the current date against the DST schedules to be sure!
